record.question: A joint that becomes twists and turns on itself is called:
record.explanation: Printed page 6 confirms the malformed wording "becomes twists and turns on itself" without further clarification. Sprain is the most defensible intended answer because twisting a joint can stretch or tear its ligaments; strain concerns muscle or tendon, while dislocation and subluxation require joint displacement. Confidence is low because the printed stem does not explicitly describe ligament injury (definition corroborated by NIAMS: https://www.niams.nih.gov/health-topics/sports-injuries).
